references.text: The same age limit of twenty years and older is used in the census of Israel's men who were fit to serve in the army.
The age limit of twenty years and older is mentioned again in connection with those struck by God's judgment in the wilderness.
The second census in Israel uses the same age limit of twenty years and older.
Ransom money was collected as a gift to the Lord, following a principle similar to the ransom tax.
The immediate context explains the purpose of the ransom tax and the amount that was to be given.
It shows the implementation of the collection of ransom money from those who were twenty years old and older.
King Joash ordered the collection of the annual tax that Moses had imposed, a reference to this ransom tax.
Jesus and the temple tax—the two-drachma tax that was required was based on this Mosaic ordinance.
Complementary principles for giving: a fixed duty based on age versus a proportional gift based on blessing.
